issues.problem: This mixes non-standard and standard quantities. K > 1 follows from $E^\circ_{cell} > 0$ (equivalently $\Delta G^\circ < 0$), not from $E_{cell} > 0$. A reaction can have $E_{cell} > 0$ under given concentrations while K < 1.
issues.correction: $E_{cell} > 0$ and $\Delta G < 0$ mean the reaction is spontaneous under the given conditions. Separately, $E^\circ_{cell} > 0$ and $\Delta G^\circ < 0$ mean K > 1.

issues.quote: Alkali metals are always $+1$ and alkaline earth metals are always $+2$
issues.problem: Saying 'always' contradicts the rule given just before it, that the ON of an element in its free state is 0. The rule applies only to compounds.
issues.correction: In all their compounds, alkali metals have ON +1 and alkaline earth metals have ON +2.
